keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Union of Saxe-Gotha and Saxe-Altenburg: 1672'. Altenburg circle 12.43E 50.99N 20 km; Saalfeld circle 11.37E 50.65N 12 km, soft (the lands lost on 24 February 1680). Revised after review: the 1672-1679 shape has only Gotha, Altenburg and the Saalfeld lands. The five other 1680 shares (Coburg, Meiningen, Römhild, Eisenberg, Hildburghausen) are left out on purpose: the Gotha page does not list them or say when they came to Ernest the Pious (it dates the duchy 1672 and Altenburg 1675 in the ruler list and the partition 'on 24 February 1680' only for the whole), and the Saxe-Coburg page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxe-Coburg) names only Albrecht's Coburg, the separation of Römhild and Hildburghausen and Meiningen's sovereignty, without a 1672 acquisition; none of the five duchies has a dossier in this batch, so a 1680 loss would have no mirror. The map therefore shows less than the combined Ernestine lands of 1672-1680 (a gap, listed in the notes).

New keyframe: 'the Principality was divided on 24 February 1680 among his seven surviving sons'; 'The lands of Saxe-Saalfeld went to the youngest of them'. The other five shares are unnamed on the page and not removed.

New keyframe: 'gained further Ernestine territories upon the death of Duke Albert V of Saxe-Coburg in 1699'. The page names no territory; the 10 km Coburg circle (10.96E 50.26N) is a stand-in. Revised after review: the Saxe-Coburg page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saxe-Coburg) says only that after Albert's death in 1699 'This was followed by the usual inheritance disputes', a 35-year dispute between Saxe-Meiningen and Saxe-Saalfeld, and that Saxe-Saalfeld was united with 'the remaining territories of Saxe-Coburg' in 1735; no page names the share Gotha received, so the circle stays a stand-in at confidence 1 and is taken away in 1735 (next keyframe).

New keyframe: further territories on the death of Duke Christian of Saxe-Eisenberg in 1707 (circle 11.90E 50.97N 10 km). About 3,140 km2 in circles against the page's 1800 area of 3,007 km2. Revised after review: ends 1734; from 1735 the Coburg stand-in circle belongs to Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld (its dossier draws the same circle from 6 August 1735).

ledger.note: 1640: the Ernestinische Teilung. Ernest I 'received the newly established Duchy of Saxe-Gotha' when the sons of Duke John II 'divided their paternal heritage'. (The page: 'nominally created in 1672' and 'proper came into existence in 1680'.)

1672: Saxe-Altenburg. Infobox 'Union of Saxe-Gotha and Saxe-Altenburg: 1672'; 'Ernest the Pious, by his marriage with Elisabeth Sophie, inherited the major part of his possessions' (the text also says 'inherited Saxe-Altenburg in 1675').

24 February 1680: Saalfeld. 'the Principality was divided on 24 February 1680 among his seven surviving sons. The lands of Saxe-Saalfeld went to the youngest of them' (Gotha page: 'Ernest's combined duchy was divided again after his death in 1675'). The other five shares are not named.

1699: Coburg. 'gained further Ernestine territories upon the death of Duke Albert V of Saxe-Coburg in 1699' (page silent on which territory; the Coburg page says the dispute 'was not settled until 1735'). Review follow-up: the Saxe-Coburg page was opened and does not divide Albert V's lands; it names the Meiningen-Saalfeld dispute (35 years, to 1735), Sonnefeld to Saxe-Hildburghausen in 1707 and Neuhaus am Rennweg and Sonneberg to Saxe-Meiningen. The Coburg circle is therefore a stand-in at confidence 1 and is lost in 1735.
1707: Eisenberg. 'gained further Ernestine territories upon the death of ... Duke Christian of Saxe-Eisenberg in 1707' (the page names no territory).

6 August 1735: the Coburg stand-in leaves the state. The Coburg-Saalfeld page gives the date on which Saxe-Saalfeld took the Saxe-Coburg properties (its dossier's 1735 gain, month 8) and the Saxe-Coburg page says the Meiningen-Saalfeld dispute lasted 35 years and Saalfeld was united with 'the remaining territories of Saxe-Coburg'. No page says Gotha held Coburg proper, so this loss mirrors the 1699 stand-in and is confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1826: Altenburg. 'Saxe-Altenburg was given to the Duke of Saxe-Hildburghausen' by the arbitration of King Frederick Augustus I of Saxony (the Altenburg circle is a stand-in).

1826: the line is extinct. 'the house of Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg finally became extinct in 1825'; 'As a result of an arbitration issued by King Frederick Augustus I of Saxony in 1826' Saxe-Gotha 'passed to the Duchy of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld', which formed the new Saxe-Coburg and Gotha. Revised after review: the Coburg stand-in circle is no longer in the hand-over (lost 1735).

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (2 pages; budget 1-3). New state: Cliopatria has no pre-1806 Saxon-duchy rows.

SCOPE. The state starts with Saxe-Gotha in 1640 and ends in 1826, when the arbitration of the King of Saxony redistributed the lands (the line was extinct in 1825). Cliopatria's saxe-altenburg (1806-70) and saxe-coburg-and-gotha (1836-39) rows overlap the last twenty years, and the reviewer should decide which side carries 1806-26. The page is silent on wars; the 1675 division and the five other shares of 1680 (Coburg, Meiningen, Romhild, Eisenberg, Hildburghausen) are not named on the Gotha page; the Coburg-Saalfeld page names Saalfeld alone.

SHAPES. Gotha 10.72E 50.95N 20 km; Altenburg 12.43E 50.99N 20 km; Saalfeld 11.37E 50.65N 12 km; Coburg 10.96E 50.26N 10 km; Eisenberg 11.90E 50.97N 10 km. About 3,140 km2 for the 1707 shape. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Gotha', 'Altenburg', 'Saalfeld', 'Coburg', 'Eisenberg (Thuringia)'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) 1672 or 1675 for Altenburg; (2) the unnamed territories of 1699 and 1707; (3) the 1826 redistribution is stated in two sentences only; (4) the Coburg page's infobox gives 11 February 1826 and its text 12 November 1826.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: Saxe-Altenburg (1603-1672 and after 1826), Saxe-Hildburghausen, Saxe-Meiningen and the other 1680 duchies.

REVISION 2026-10-25 (after review). (1) Coburg drawn twice: the 1699 stand-in circle at Coburg stayed to 1825 while duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld draws the same circle from 6 August 1735. The Saxe-Coburg page was opened: it does not say what Gotha received in 1699 (only 'the usual inheritance disputes' and a 35-year Meiningen-Saalfeld dispute), so the share cannot be moved to a better place from the pages; the stand-in is kept at confidence 1 to 1734 and a 1735 loss to duchy-of-saxe-coburg-saalfeld (month 8, confidence 1) is entered, K4 split at 1735, the Coburg circle taken out of the 1826 hand-over. The Coburg-Saalfeld dossier's 1735 gain names counterpart 'Saxe-Coburg (extinct 1699; no dossier)' and not this dossier (not touched in this repair). (2) 1672-1680: the five other shares are left out and the K1 note says why; GAP: Coburg, Meiningen, Römhild, Eisenberg and Hildburghausen are undrawn 1672-1680. (3) The Saxe-Coburg page's 24 February 1680 matches the month-2 loss of Saalfeld; it names Frederick I, not Frederick II, as administrator of Saxe-Gotha in 1680.
